newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close flat ahead of employment data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close flat ahead of employment data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed on Thursday, ceding gains made earlier in the session as investors shifted their focus to tomorrow's key Canadian and U.S. employment data, analysts said.

"The wind has been taken completely out of the market until the (U.S.) non-farm number tomorrow morning. Everyone has just positioned themselves already," said Philip Strathy, chief investment officer with Strathy Investments Ltd.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.02 to C$110.78 to yield 7.089 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.76 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was 33 basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close.

Tomorrow's Canadian and U.S. employment data, especially the U.S. non-farms payroll report, has been eagerly anticipated by the market for several weeks now. The data is seen as a solid indicator of economic growth in both countries. There is concern a strong U.S. report could be the harbinger of a rate increase by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
In Canada, economists surveyed by Reuters have forecast that Canada's unemployment rate will fall to 9.6 percent in January from 9.7 percent a month earlier.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it plans to auction on February 12 C$2.3 billion of bonds with a coupon of 7.25 percent and maturing on June 1, 2007.
The Bank of Canada said it will buy at least C$345 million of the new bonds. The new bonds are in addition to C$4.8 billion bonds due June 2007 outstanding.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.08 to C$104.23 to yield 6.41 percent.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.87 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.13 percent.
